implementation_summary: StepKind 'compaction' added on both sides and in STEP_KINDS; Conversation.forkedFrom added. onCompaction payload is stashed in streamConversationResponse; only after stopStreamRef ownership is confirmed and the original's chat.done steps are applied does the hook build the fork (pure buildFork in src/lib/fork.ts), hand it to onFork (addForkedConversation: prepend + select) and void-call streamConversationResponse(fork, {withoutCompactContext, contextRequest}) so the fork takes stopStreamRef before the original's finally (no clear, no extra settledCount bump). Fork = original's system steps + one compaction step, inherited settings/tools, '<title> (compacted)', titleEdited true, empty requestContexts. Sidebar shows user-or-compaction conversations; transcript treats compaction as a visible turn boundary; compaction card (theme-token background, header 'written by <model> via compact_context', no inspect action) with back-link above it.
decisions: findLastDeletableStepIndex does not treat compaction as deletable (it is a boundary in findResponseStartIndex/deleteLastExchangeCutIndex only) so AC-FORK-12 holds and a compaction-only fork has nothing to delete.
Fork built from the send-time conversation snapshot (title/settings at send).

Fork's first send gets the context fields captured at the original's send, passed explicitly; tools filtered by name for that request only, the fork's activeToolIds still include compact_context for the next user send.

compaction content = summary + optional '

Remaining work:
' section; rendered via markdown branch when enabled (react-markdown, no raw HTML).
Back-link: Transcript props forkOrigin/onOpenConversation (chat-workspace edits thin); plain text when the original was deleted.
Fork orchestration is not awaited by the original's promise chain.
caveats: AC-STRUCT-3 release gate not run here (lead runs it).
Fork inherits send-time settings if the user edits the original while compaction streams.
AC-STRUCT-3 release-gate part verified at epic AC-closure (lead runs the release gate)
